sections.h2: Where is Logan County and what is it like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Logan County sits in central Illinois between Springfield, Bloomington, Peoria and Decatur, and its seat is Lincoln. The county was established in 1839 and covers about 618 square miles of land. In 1845 a piece of De Witt County was added, which gave it its present shape. Neighbors are Mason, Tazewell, McLean, De Witt, Macon, Sangamon and Menard counties.

Lincoln is the largest city, and Atlanta and Mount Pulaski are the other two cities. Lincoln was founded in 1853 along the Chicago and Mississippi Railroad and is described as the first city named for Abraham Lincoln while he was still a lawyer. I-55 links it to Bloomington and Springfield, Amtrak stops at Lincoln Station, and the state's Logan Correctional Center sits just outside the city in unincorporated Logan County.

Lincoln's January mean temperature is about 26 degrees and its July mean about 75, so a house here goes through hard freezes and humid summers. Roofs, gutters and basements are the usual inspection items.

sections.h2: Which Logan County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The county's Treasurer page divides the work among three offices in Lincoln, and the split tells you where to call.

  • Supervisor of Assessments: instructs the township assessors, keeps tax maps and property record cards, serves as clerk of the Board of Review and grants exemptions. The office is at 122 N. McLean St., phone 217-732-9635.
  • County Clerk: extends the rates over each taxing district's levy and handles redemption of tax sale certificates. The office is in Room 20 of the courthouse, phone 217-732-4148.
  • County Treasurer: mails the bills, collects the tax, tracks granted assessment appeals and disburses money to the taxing bodies. The office is in Room 11 of the courthouse, phone 217-732-3761.

The Treasurer also serves as ex officio county collector, and that covers real estate, mobile home and drainage tax. Everyone in the county pays county, township and road and bridge tax, and the school and fire districts on top of those depend on which side of a boundary your parcel falls.

sections.h2: What are the Logan County tax dates for the 2025 tax year?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's page lists the 2025 tax year, payable in 2026, as follows. These dates have all passed, and the same sequence repeats each year with new dates.

  • Real estate bills mailed May 8, 2026.
  • First installment due June 15, 2026, and second installment due September 1, 2026, each with a penalty of 1.5% added per month if unpaid.
  • Mobile home bills mailed March 30, 2026, due June 1, 2026, with a $25 penalty after that date and $25 more each month, up to $100.
  • Tax sale held October 29, 2026 at 9:00 a.m., with buyer registration closing October 16, 2026.

The page says that Logan County, under Public Act 104-0553, elected to acquire delinquent real estate taxes as trustee for the taxing districts. If your taxes are unpaid after a due date, the Treasurer asks you to call for the current amount rather than relying on the bill, since penalty keeps accruing.

sections.h2: How do you pay a Logan County tax bill?
sections.html:
Every payment method requires the tax payment stub from the bill. The Treasurer's page lists these options:

  • In person at Room 11 of the courthouse, by cash or check. Debit and credit cards are accepted for real estate only, with a fee of 2.35% plus $1.50.
  • A drop box on N. Kickapoo St. across from Latham Park, or boxes on the north and south sides of the courthouse. Do not leave cash.
  • Most Logan County banks, with the exception of Regions and CEFCU.
  • By mail, where the postmark counts as the date received. To avoid penalty, postmark on or before the due date.
  • By card or e-check over the phone at 217-203-8359, using the property index number, or through the online link on the Treasurer's page.

A bill that never arrives is still owed. The state statute treats a mailed payment postmarked by the required date as timely, and the first installment is delinquent after the later of June 1 or the day after the printed due date (35 ILCS 200/21-15).

sections.h2: How is a Logan County home assessed and how is the bill built?
sections.html:
The county and township assessors set the assessed value, and the abstract goes to the state, which may apply a multiplier that raises, lowers or leaves values unchanged. The County Clerk then divides each taxing body's levy by its assessed valuation to get a rate, capped by statute where a limit applies. The total rate is multiplied by the equalized assessed value to produce the tax.

Illinois sets the assessment level at one-third of market value. The Supervisor of Assessments applies equalization factors to keep values at 33 1/3%, and the Board of Review rules say all property is reassessed every four years, though the assessor may reassess yearly. The 2026 assessment preamble and publication ran in the Lincoln Courier on Friday, October 2, 2026, and the office's page links to a PDF of it.

Logan County also registers mobile homes through the Supervisor of Assessments. Taxes must be paid and the title valid before registration, and a tax certificate from the Treasurer is needed to transfer a title through the Secretary of State.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Logan County assessment?
sections.html:
The Board of Review rules set the deadline at 30 days from publication of assessment changes for your township. Complaints and evidence must reach the assessment office by 4:30 p.m. or carry a postmark on or before the deadline. Talking to the assessor does not extend the 30 days.

The rules add several requirements that trip people up:

  • File a separate complaint for each parcel, on the Board's form. Fax and email are not accepted.
  • Attach one copy of all supporting evidence to the complaint. A complaint marked as having no evidence will likely receive a decision of no change.
  • You cannot protest the amount of taxes, only the assessment, on the grounds listed on the form.
  • A missing item draws a notice and 10 days to supply it.
  • A hearing is by appointment and gives about 15 minutes, and no new evidence is taken at the hearing.

The Board meets on or before the first Monday of June, and its three members are appointed by the County Board. Each owner receives a written tentative decision, and a request for a hearing must be made within the period stated on it.

sections.h2: Which exemptions does Logan County list?
sections.html:
The Supervisor of Assessments lists these exemptions, and its office verifies eligibility, which can mean proof each year:

  • General homestead: a $6,000 reduction in assessed value for owners who live in the home.
  • Senior citizen: an additional $5,000 for owners 65 or older, with proof of age.
  • Senior assessment freeze: locks the value at the qualifying year for owners already getting the senior exemption, with household gross income of $65,000 or less in assessment year 2025 and $75,000 or less beginning with 2026.
  • Homestead improvement: exempts the added value of a garage, porch or deck on an owner-occupied home for four years.
  • Returning veterans: $5,000 off the principal residence for two consecutive years.
  • Disabled veterans: $2,500 for a 30 to 49% service-connected rating, $5,000 for 50 to 69%, and full exemption at 70% or more.
  • Disabled persons: a $2,000 reduction with annual proof.

State law matches the first two amounts (35 ILCS 200/15-175 and 15-170) for a county that is not next to a county of 3,000,000 or more people.

sections.h2: What should a Logan County seller do about the tax bill?
sections.html:
Pull the parcel on the county's tax search and compare it with the bill in your hand, then ask the Treasurer for the current amount due on any open installment. At closing the title company prorates the year between you and the buyer, and the settlement statement shows which installment is paid, owed or escrowed. If the lender escrows taxes, confirm what it has already paid.

A house with unpaid prior years is the harder case. Ask the County Clerk whether the taxes were sold and what the redemption figure is, because a certificate holder must be paid before title can clear. State law generally allows 3 years from the sale date for redemption, with exceptions (35 ILCS 200/21-350).

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Logan County Treasurer?
faqs.a: 217-732-3761. The office is in Room 11 of the Logan County Courthouse in Lincoln, and the Treasurer's page directs people with questions about a bill or a late amount to call that number.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Logan County real estate tax?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's page states a penalty of 1.5% added per month if a first or second installment is not paid by its due date. For mobile homes, the penalty is $25 after June 1 and $25 more per month, up to $100.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Logan County tax bill with a card?
faqs.a: Yes, for real estate tax, at the Treasurer's office, over the phone at 217-203-8359 or online. The page lists a fee of 2.35% plus $1.50 for in-person card payments, and you need the property index number.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Logan County assessment?
faqs.a: 30 days from the publication of assessment changes for your township. Complaints must arrive by 4:30 p.m. or be postmarked by the deadline, and each parcel needs its own form with evidence attached.

faqs.q: Who grants the general homestead exemption in Logan County?
faqs.a: The Supervisor of Assessments, at 122 N. McLean St. in Lincoln or 217-732-9635. The office lists the general homestead exemption as a $6,000 reduction in assessed value for owners who live in the property.
